answer: Pay a voyage data grant per inspected vessel. A port registry binds a tamper-resistant transponder to each hull; the device signs a fresh signal and a log of anchor movements. Record each payment against the hull ID, and deactivate an old transponder before certifying its replacement. Operating a thousand agent keys on one boat still yields one grant. Expanding the farm requires leasing more vessels and paying inspection and upkeep costs. This assumes honest hull inspections, keys that cannot be cloned, and grants below the cost of maintaining extra boats.
